**Format:** Lecture + mini-project

## Topics covered
- Correlation vs causation — industry examples where the confusion cost money
- Confounders: why the data lies and how to spot it
- A/B test design: hypothesis formulation, control group, sample size calculation
- Statistical significance as a business decision — not just a p-value checkbox
- Early stopping, peeking, and why companies lose money from it
- Observational methods when experiments aren't possible (difference-in-differences, intro)

## Mini-project
Scenario: a SaaS company is considering a pricing page redesign. Students:
1. Design the A/B test (write the hypothesis, calculate required sample size and test duration)
2. Receive pre-given results and interpret them
3. Make the launch / no-launch call and justify it in a one-page business memo

## Tools
`scipy.stats`, `pingouin` — students must understand the numbers, not just run functions

## Deliverable
- A/B test design document
- Launch decision memo (graded on business reasoning, not statistical fluency alone)
